records.issue_text: [BUG] Init's initialization work (per the surrounding code, s.initErr is assigned inside a goroutine that runs asynchronously) is now checked exactly once in the constructor, and every per-request `s.Init(ctx)` error check has been deleted, so a background init failure is never surfaced to callers again. When the background search-index init or initWatcher fails after NewResourceServer returns nil error, Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search all proceed against a half-initialized server (no watcher running, missing/stale index) and return wrong-but-plausible results instead of the error they previously returned via the per-request Init check.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering initWatcher() to run after s.search.init(ctx) drops write events that occur during index construction, leaving the search index permanently stale for those resources. A dashboard created/updated while the initial index build is running (builds take seconds-to-minutes on large tenants, as the init log of duration_secs shows) is never written to the index because no watcher is registered yet; the event has no WrittenEvent record and is not replayed, so Search returns stale/missing results until a full restart reindexes.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Narrowing cacheMu in BuildIndex from the whole call to just the cache write removes the mutual exclusion that previously serialized concurrent index builds, so concurrent builders for the same key race on the bleve directory and cache entry. searchSupport.init builds in a spawned goroutine (init returns while building continues per the `}()` before the duration log) while handleEvent can call getOrCreateIndex concurrently; two BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource both pass the nil-cache check, both write the same on-disk bleve directory (file-threshold path), and one index instance is silently discarded, so events applied to the discarded index are lost from search results.
records.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go`, `BuildIndex` previously held `b.cacheMu` for the entire call (`b.cacheMu.Lock(); defer b.cacheMu.Unlock()`), but the diff removes that and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This change eliminates mutual exclusion during index creation (including `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on the on-disk path), so concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same `NamespacedResource` can race while creating/writing the same directory and whichever finishes last will win the cache entry. records.issue_text: [BUG] Removing the cacheMu lock from around the whole BuildIndex body allows two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key to run simultaneously, and the last writer to b.cache[key] wins regardless of which build had the fresher data. Concurrent getOrCreateIndex misses for the same key each build a full Bleve index (duplicate CPU/memory spike), and if the older-RV build finishes last it overwrites the cache entry, serving a stale index with no error signal; the previous global lock serialized this and made the first build authoritative.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The watcher and search-index background loops now inherit the context passed into NewResourceServer rather than a context owned by the server's lifetime. If the caller passes a request-scoped or otherwise cancellable context to the constructor, the watcher and index event consumer are cancelled the moment that context is done, and because no method re-runs Init anymore, the server serves stale data for the rest of the process lifetime with no log at the call sites that removed the Init guard.
records.rationale: The diff makes initialization context come from the constructor and removes all per-RPC Init guards. In `NewResourceServer(...)`, it now does `err := s.Init(ctx)` before returning, and later RPCs no longer call `s.Init(ctx)` (removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob). In `searchSupport.init(ctx)` the code starts a goroutine (`go func() { ... }()`) after starting a span, and `ctx` is now explicitly re-assigned from `s.tracer.Start(...)` (`ctx, span := ...`), making it more likely that this `ctx` is the one captured by any background work

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the full-duration cacheMu lock from BuildIndex allows two concurrent builds for the same key to both construct indexes, with the second cache write overwriting the first while callers of the first index keep a stale object. Two concurrent getOrCreateIndex misses (e.g., two simultaneous Search requests for a cold resource after startup-init races) now each build a full bleve index; the loser's in-memory handle diverges from the cache, so events applied via the cached index are invisible to the holder of the overwritten one and vice versa, producing inconsistent search results and duplicated memory/file handles (two bleve indexes on the same on-disk directory when above FileThreshold, where the loser also holds an open file index). Previously the mutex serialized builds, making this impossible.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Removing the cacheMu hold for the duration of BuildIndex allows two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key to both complete full index builds, with the second writer overwriting the first's entry in b.cache. During concurrent first-access initialization of the same NamespacedResource, CPU and memory are double-spent on full bleve index builds, and an index handle already handed to a reader via the first store is silently orphaned (its documents never receive watcher updates since the watcher is registered against whichever instance the second call returns), producing a stale/un-updating search index for that resource until restart. The final map write is locked, but the check-then-build-then-publish sequence is not atomic.

Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource key now both proceed past the removed lock and can create two bleve indexes (two writers to the same on-disk directory when size > FileThreshold), with the loser's index silently overwriting the winner in b.cache and a possible file-handle conflict on the persistent directory. records.issue_text: [BUG] Reordering Init so the search index is fully built before initWatcher() starts means writes committed to the SQL backend during the (potentially minutes-long) index build are never delivered to the index, leaving it permanently stale for those keys. A dashboard saved while init is still building indexes produces no watcher event for that snapshot; the search index serves stale/missing results for that resource until a full reindex or another write to the same key occurs, so users see outdated search results after the very startup this diff slows down with the now-synchronous Init.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Moving initWatcher() to run after search.init() opens an unobserved-write window: search.init() builds the index from a DB snapshot, and any writes committed after that snapshot but before initWatcher() starts are never delivered to the index. Resources created/updated while a large index is building (the exact time index building is slow) are permanently missing from the search index until the next restart or rebuild — searches silently return stale results with no error surfaced anywhere; previously the watcher was registered first, so events during the build were captured.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] On the file-backed path, if the builder callback or any step after `bleve.New(dir, ...)` succeeds but a later step returns an error, the created on-disk bleve index is never closed or cleaned up. Repeated failed builds leave orphaned index directories and open file descriptors under b.opts.Root; the pre-existing `size > FileThreshold` check means large tenants hit this on every retry, eventually exhausting file handles on the server.
